chapter_theme: A single song at Thiruvambar (திருவம்பர்) in the Chola land: the poet, who did not seek the light, mantra and inner space, but gambled, raced horses and danced for pleasure until the senses failed, asks when the trouble of the burning ground will end; the praise sets the peacock leaping across the cosmic circles.

805.reading: The poet says that, without taking hold of the light, the mantra, the teaching and the open space where the golden flower blooms, he talked of gambling and wagers, of five breeds of horses leaping in the street circuits, dressed up and danced for pleasure until his eyes grew dim and his five senses shrank, and that when the term written on the leaf by Brahma is reached, men run to the burning ground, fall and are burnt; he asks when this trouble will end. The praise has the peacock leap over the circles of sun, moon and sea and search the cosmos, the dust of the deceivers' realm fly to the sky while Murugan smiles, and Murugan infatuated with the forest girl, lord of Ambar in the Chola land where Indra and the gods worship.
805.nuance: சோதி மந்திரம் போதகம் ... வெளி தோடு அலர்ந்த பொன் பூ இருந்த இடம்: the first lines seem to name the yogic goals, the inner light, the mantra, the open space and the golden lotus, which the poet failed to reach. The second half is built on மண்டலம் (circles of sun and moon, of the sea, of the cosmos), perhaps also the yogic circles. The lines on gambling and horses (அஞ்சுவகை சாதி, சிந்துபரி) are hard to divide.
